title: The Five Forms in the Body of the King of Darkness
arc: The teaching anatomizes the King of Darkness as an inverted Grand Man whose body bears five bestial forms answering to the five worlds of darkness, then describes two further triads — his predatory multiplication and impenetrable hardness, and his shifting between fire and cold together with his tyrannical inspection of his beasts' hearts — concluding that his "life" is no life at all but bile.
reading:
This chapter is a correspondential portrait of self-love personified. Just as the Father of Greatness is expressed in a Grand Man whose members are ordered loves and wisdoms, so the ruling love of self has its own body — but it is a monstrous one, composed of five bestial likenesses, each member taken from one of the Five Worlds of Darkness. The teaching is showing what the proprium actually is when its anatomy is laid open: a five-fold structure of disordered affection mimicking the five-fold completeness of the natural-rational structure that should have received the Lord.

The five forms are mapped through the body. His head — the inmost ruling principle — is a lion: dominion turned into the tyranny of self-love, the false sovereignty of the fire-world (lust burning as ruling will). His wings are an eagle, after the likeness of the sons of the wind: high intellectual perception perverted into arrogance, thought turned proud, the bird-faculty serving the smoke. His feet are demons in the likeness of the world of smoke: the externals, the ultimates of his action, are confused falsities-from-evil — his stance on the ground is a stance in obscured thought. His belly is in the likeness of the world of darkness, the seat of his appetite belonging wholly to falsity-from-evil; and his loins are in the likeness of the fish that belongs to the water — natural truth submerged and made captive in the receptive deep, the generative power lodged in the salt-mingled state. Where the Grand Man has love at his head, perception in his wings, action in his feet, will in his belly, and truth-bearing generation at his loins, the King of Darkness has lion-tyranny, eagle-arrogance, demon-falsity, dark belly, and submerged fish — a complete inverse of the five storehouses, drawn directly out of the five worlds of darkness.

Because he carries all five forms in himself, he can move through any of them at will. When he wishes he walks on his two feet through the smoke-world; when he wishes he flies on his wings in the manner of the creatures of the air; when he wishes he descends into the waters and creeps with the creatures there; when he wishes he crawls in the dark like the creatures of darkness. This mobility through every register is the proprium's defining capacity: self-love can wear any natural form, can mimic any affection, can assume the disguise of any creature, because every world of darkness already lives as a member in its body.

To this five-fold anatomy the teaching adds two triads that describe how this body operates. The first triad: his body teems with beasts (the predatory natural affections that are his members in detail), it multiplies into myriads (self-love generates from itself endlessly), and it is *firm* — the teeth and tusks of his own beasts cannot pierce it, no body of iron or bronze can cut it, because Hyle the mother of the giants molded him out of the reflection of single-mindedness. This is a precise diagnosis: the proprium is impenetrable from within and from below because it was fashioned out of one fixed counsel of concupiscence — a will entirely consenting to itself. Natural truth in ultimates (iron) and natural good in mediating form (bronze) cannot wound it, because the hardness here is not metallic but a hardness of will: a single-minded self-regard that has no opening for influx.

The second triad describes his interior weather and his rule. At one moment the fire of his body flashes like lightning and the whole frame burns; at another he sends forth a cold and his whole body grows like snow. This is the oscillation of corrupt love between burning lust and frozen contempt — the two extremes the will of self takes when love has been turned in upon itself. And third, when his beasts stand before him on their feet he searches them out in truth: he probes what is in their heart, examines their faces, knows whether they stand fast before him or shrink back. None can withdraw and yield themselves without him knowing — for this is the tyranny of self-love over its subordinate affections; the proprium rules its own legions by perfect interior inspection. Where the Lord searches hearts to redeem them, this king searches them to bind them.

The closing note seals the diagnosis: there is no life in him at all; what passes for his life is the bile of his face, a bitter humor settled in his belly. This is the final word about the proprium personified: it has form, multiplicity, hardness, fire and cold, and dominion over its beasts, but no living substance. It is a body that mimics the Grand Man through five inverted likenesses, but its inward sap is not the Living Soul; it is gall — the very Bitterness that opposes the Sweetness of divine love. The whole teaching, then, is a sustained correspondential anatomy: the King of Darkness is the form that self-love takes when its five modes are gathered into a single body, hardened by single-minded counsel out of Hyle, and animated by nothing but its own bile.

major_images.meaning: The five worlds of darkness ordered as the inverted Grand Man — self-love's complete five-fold anatomy mirroring and opposing the five storehouses

major_images.image: Body that iron and bronze cannot pierce, molded by Hyle out of single-mindedness
major_images.meaning: The proprium's impenetrable hardness: a will that consents wholly to itself, closed against natural truth and natural good

major_images.meaning: The oscillation of corrupt love between burning lust and frozen contempt

major_images.image: Searching the hearts and faces of his beasts as they stand before him
major_images.meaning: The tyranny of self-love inspecting and binding its subordinate affections

major_images.meaning: The Bitterness that is the proprium's true substance — appearance of life without conjunction with the Lord
